name: queracode
description: The Quera workbench for VS Code — browse and solve problems, submit and read judge results, and author lessons, problems and judges in Persian/RTL Markdown, with validators and AI assistance built in.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Welcome to QueraCode — the Quera workbench.

[Sign in to Quera](command:queracode.login)

Sign in with your Quera username and password, or paste a session id, then browse and solve problems right here.

[Open the dashboard](command:queracode.openDashboard)
[Take the tour](command:queracode.openWalkthrough)

Your Quera colleges and classes appear here once you sign in.

[Sign in to Quera](command:queracode.login)

Contests you can enter appear here once you sign in.

Submissions you make from VS Code are listed here.

Open a problem and send a solution to see its judge result.

queracode.baseUrl.description: Quera base URL. Override only if you proxy Quera.

enumDescriptions: Use a pre-issued session_id cookie (stored in VS Code SecretStorage).
Sign in with a username/password (exchanged for a session).
queracode.authMethod.markdownDescription: Which sign-in QueraCode offers by default. Run **Quera: Sign In** to switch — credentials always go to VS Code's SecretStorage, never to `settings.json`.

queracode.username.markdownDescription: Quera account identifier — the email address or mobile number you sign in with. The password lives in SecretStorage.

queracode.defaultLanguage.description: Default language when creating a solution (python, cpp, java, go, ...).

queracode.editorDirection.description: Text direction for the problem/lesson preview and editors.

queracode.persianFont.description: Font stack for Persian (RTL) text in webviews.

queracode.latinFont.description: Font stack for Latin text in webviews.

queracode.monoFont.description: Monospace font for code in webviews.

queracode.enableSubmission.markdownDescription: Allow sending solutions to Quera. Off by default because a submission consumes an attempt and appears on scoreboards.

queracode.enableWrite.markdownDescription: Allow changing Quera content — publishing درسنامه, editing assignment problems, uploading media. Off by default.

queracode.readOnly.markdownDescription: Master switch. When on, it forces `#queracode.enableSubmission#` and `#queracode.enableWrite#` off regardless of their own values.

queracode.sandbox.markdownDescription: How solutions run against sample tests. `docker` isolates the run and is recommended; `local` executes directly on your machine; `none` only prints the command.

queracode.problemsetPageSize.description: How many problems to show per page in the Problemset view.

queracode.solutionsDir.markdownDescription: Workspace subfolder QueraCode writes into: solutions, saved problems, generated tests and downloaded projects.

queracode.autoRegisterMcp.description: Write .vscode/mcp.json on startup to register the sibling QueraMCP server for MCP-capable coder agents (it will then appear under 'MCP Servers' in the Extensions view). Off by default — QueraCode itself never needs it; run 'Quera: Register QueraMCP for Coder Agents' to opt in once.

enumDescriptions: Groq — very fast inference for open models.
Google Gemini via its OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
LM Studio (local) — no API key required.
queracode.ai.provider.markdownDescription: Provider for the **Quera AI** commands. Run **Quera AI: Configure AI Provider** to store the key in SecretStorage; it is never written to settings.

queracode.ai.model.markdownDescription: Model id for the chosen provider. Blank uses that provider's default.

queracode.ai.baseUrl.markdownDescription: Base URL override — required when `#queracode.ai.provider#` is `custom` (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint).

queracode.openDashboardOnStartup.description: Open the Quera dashboard automatically when VS Code starts (off by default).

queracode.customCss.markdownDescription: CSS injected into every QueraCode webview — bring your own `@font-face`, colors and sizes.

queracode.fontSize.description: Base font size (px) for Quera panels and previews.

queracode.accentColor.markdownDescription: Override the Quera cyan used across panels, as `#RRGGBB`. Leave empty for Quera's own `#0099CC`.

queracode.repo.autoPull.markdownDescription: Fast-forward the linked Quera course repository on a timer. Skipped whenever the working tree is dirty or mid-merge, so it can never overwrite local work.

queracode.repo.autoPullIntervalMinutes.markdownDescription: How often to fast-forward, in minutes. Requires `#queracode.repo.autoPull#`.

queracode.repo.autoPush.markdownDescription:
Commit and push saved changes in the course repository automatically.

**Pushing publishes to the live college** — the repository's GitHub Actions workflow syncs changed lessons to Quera. Requires `#queracode.enableWrite#`.

queracode.repo.autoPushDelaySeconds.markdownDescription: Quiet period after the last save before auto-push commits, so a burst of saves becomes one commit.

queracode.repo.branch.markdownDescription: Branch auto-commits land on. It is checked out first, and created from the current HEAD if it does not exist. Leave empty to use whatever is already checked out.

queracode.repo.commitMessage.markdownDescription: Commit message template. `${files}` lists the changed lesson folders, `${count}` how many, `${date}` the timestamp.

queracode.sync.autoPublishOnSave.markdownDescription:
Publish a bound Markdown file straight to Quera every time you save it.

**Students see the change immediately** — there is no review step. Requires `#queracode.enableWrite#`, and only affects files bound with **Quera: Bind File to a Quera درسنامه/تمرین**.

queracode.sync.publishDelaySeconds.markdownDescription: Quiet period after the last save before auto-publish fires, so saving repeatedly while editing publishes once.

queracode.sync.confirmBeforePublish.markdownDescription: Ask before a manual publish. Auto-publish never asks — that is what makes it automatic, which is why it is off by default.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with QueraCode
walkthroughs.description: Sign in to Quera, solve your first problem, and author lessons and judges — without leaving VS Code.

steps.title: Sign in to Quera
steps.description:
Sign in with your Quera username and password. If your account uses a one-time code, Google or GitHub, paste a session id instead — QueraCode offers both.
Credentials go to VS Code's SecretStorage, never to settings.json.
[Sign in to Quera](command:queracode.login)

media.altText: The QueraCode activity bar with the problemset, courses and submissions views

steps.title: Find a problem
steps.description:
The Problemset view carries Quera's full filter set — difficulty, tags, type, category and solve status. Search by name, or jump straight to a problem you already have a link to.
[Search problems](command:queracode.searchProblems)
[Open a problem by URL](command:queracode.openProblemByUrl)

media.altText: A Quera problem statement rendered right-to-left inside VS Code

steps.title: Solve it and run the samples
steps.description:
Scaffold a solution in your language, then run it against the problem's own sample tests in a Docker sandbox before spending an attempt.
[Run on samples](command:queracode.runSamples)

media.altText: Solve, run against samples, submit, read the judge result

steps.title: Submit and read the verdict
steps.description:
Submitting is off until you turn it on, so no attempt is ever spent by accident. Enable it, then send the active file with Ctrl+Alt+Enter and read the per-test judge breakdown in place.
[Enable submission](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22queracode.enableSubmission%22)

media.altText: What QueraCode covers end to end

steps.title: Author lessons, problems and judges
steps.description:
Write درسنامه and تمرین content in Persian Markdown with a live RTL preview, then validate the judge config, test names and Markdown before publishing.
[Start a lesson](command:queracode.newLesson)
[Scaffold a problem](command:queracode.newProblem)

media.altText: Authoring Quera content in VS Code

steps.title: Optional: bring your own AI
steps.description:
Point QueraCode at any OpenAI-compatible provider — OpenRouter, Anthropic, Groq, DeepSeek, a local Ollama, whatever you already pay for — to explain problems and review submissions. The API key lives in SecretStorage.
[Configure a provider](command:queracode.ai.configure)

media.altText: How QueraCode talks to Quera and to your AI provider

scripts.verify: npm run lint && npm run unit && npm run test:repo && npm run test:commands
scripts.verify:live: npm run verify && npm run test:live && npm run test:extension

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Running a solution against sample tests executes workspace code. In a restricted workspace QueraCode reads and renders Quera content but will not run solutions.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Browsing, reading and authoring work anywhere. Running solutions against samples needs a real filesystem.
